transcript.text: Thor! I’ve been gone for three weeks negotiating with the Dark Elves on YOUR father’s orders, and I return to THIS?! My rune-map — the one I spent months crafting — is soaked through with mead! There are scorch marks on the ceiling! You said you would keep the hall in order while I was away!

transcript.text: It seems we have some unfinished business. I apologize for the state of the hall, Loki. It was not my intention to cause such chaos. The Dark Elves and their tricks can be quite unpredictable. As for the map, I'm afraid it was accidentally damaged during our encounter with the giants. I assure you, it was not intentional. I will make it right and find a suitable replacement. Please forgive me for any inconvenience caused.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Accidentally damaged"? By *mead* and *scorched ceilings*?! Giants, you say? Last I checked, giants don't typically redecorate with ale and pyrotechnics. "Make it right"? You couldn't "make it right" if you brought me the fabric of reality itself on a silver platter! Just tell me, Thor, what *precisely* happened here? And don't you dare try to blame the Dark Elves for your inability to keep a simple promise!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your frustration, Loki. The truth is, I underestimated the chaos that would ensue from my absence. I should have anticipated the potential consequences. Thank you for your understanding. We must regroup and find a way to overcome this setback together. We are brothers, after all, and we stand together against all challenges. Trust in my word, Loki, that I will make things right.

It's not a broken drinking horn, Thor, it's a meticulously crafted artifact of immense magical significance! And now, suddenly, we're "brothers" and "stand together"? This wasn't some cosmic threat we faced, this was basic household management! You utterly, utterly failed, and now you expect me to simply... forgive and forget while my work, my *months* of work, lies ruined and sodden?
